newsitem.title: USA: Crosscomm says won't meet Q3 expectations.
newsitem.headline: Crosscomm says won't meet Q3 expectations.

text.p: CrossComm Corp said on Tuesday that revenue and operating results would be below expectations for the third quarter ended September 30, 1996.
Revenue will be about $10.8 million, reflecting lower North American sales due primarily to lower than expected sales of some of the company's new products, the company said.
The company expects to report a loss from operations of between $3.0 and $3.6 million.

Including its gain on the sales of Fore System Inc shares and interest income, the company said, it expects to report a pre-tax loss of between about $400,000 and $1 million, or $0.04 and $0.11 per share.
The company expects to report its third quarter results on October 24.
The company also said William ("BJ") Johnson, CrossComm's President, has left the company to pursue other business opportunities.
The company said it will focus on specific market segments and has created a business unit called Enterprise Products Division, to be presided over by former vice president Nigel Machin.
In a related development, CrossComm's board asked Tad Witkowicz, the company's chairman and founder, to develop plans around other products and market segments.
